01 / Selected work

Questions I'm exploring.

How can autonomous systems plan better, transfer further, and handle uncertainty?

GENERALIZATION / ACROSS ENVIRONMENTS
01VITA Lab · EPFL · Swiss AI InitiativeOngoing

Driving beyond familiar geographies

Developing a worldwide-scale evaluation benchmark to study how world models, video-action / VLA models, and end-to-end planners generalize across geographic environments.

World modelsVLAEvaluation
Sept 2026 – present
Project details

Building a modular, configuration-driven evaluation framework with model-specific adapters. It supports video-to-trajectory reconstruction, direct trajectory prediction, and configurable prediction horizons through model-specific rollout strategies.

The benchmark is part of a broader research effort on geographically generalizable world models. This is ongoing work; no completed benchmark results are claimed here.

Supervision: Valentin Gerard, Prof. Alexandre Alahi

TEMPORAL REASONING / DRIVING PLANNERS
02VITA Lab · EPFLSemester project

Giving driving planners a sense of time

Extended DrivoR with cached temporal token fusion and future scene token prediction. The best configuration improved EPDMS by 23% over the DrivoR baseline on the navmini subset.

TransformersTemporal fusionNAVSIM
Feb – June 2026
Method & evaluation scope

The temporal fusion module uses asymmetric cross-attention over historical register tokens. A second module predicts future scene tokens, inspired by latent world models and trained end-to-end without auxiliary supervision.

Evaluation scope: Training used navmini due to compute constraints. The 23% result is specific to this subset; full-scale validation on navtrain remains future work.

Supervision: Lan Feng, Prof. Alexandre Alahi

PERCEPTION UNCERTAINTY / SAFETY
03Southeast University · B.Sc. thesisITSC 2026

Testing safety when perception is imperfect

Built a reinforcement learning framework that incorporates realistic perception errors into safety-critical scenario generation. First-author paper accepted to IEEE ITSC 2026.

Reinforcement learningnuScenesBEVFusion
Nov 2024 – June 2025
Project details

Extracted distance and velocity perception-error distributions from nuScenes with BEVFusion and modeled them as sensor noise. Integrated the resulting safety risks into an RL-based scenario generation pipeline, evaluating realism, adversarial strength, and diversity.

The method generated more realistic and diverse safety-critical scenarios than perception-agnostic baselines. Supported by a Jiangsu Provincial Science and Technology Project.

Supervision: Prof. Chen Wang

04

Reinforcement learning for connected vehicle control

Developed a DQN-based shoulder-lane control strategy, evaluated in SUMO simulations of a real expressway merging section under mixed traffic.

Oct 2022 – Oct 2023

Full curriculum vitae ↗
